title: Andrew Smith, ICE-AC — 'What if the profit we optimized for was not just money, but human flourishing?'
summary: Smith coaches product and technology leaders through operating-model and transformation work. He finished Incorruptible and named the redefinition of profit as human flourishing the part he valued most, with customers, employees and communities counted in. He read the book as an argument for hope and agency, and for the claim that mission-protecting structures produce outsized value.
blockquote: What if the "profit" we optimized for was not just money, but "human flourishing?" For customers, shareholders, employees, communities, and society-at-large? I just finished Eric Ries book, Incorruptible. In it, he describes how common business practices leave companies vulnerable to losing the very thing that made them great — and goes on to show the means by which this can be prevented. But beyond this, Eric paints a picture of hope and agency. There *is* a way to preserve the mission. Companies can create *outsized value* by using structures that protect the mission. There *is* a way to influence what gets amplified. And I love this the most: defining "profit" as "human flourishing."
